questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to find a host university that both had a high academic level, taught relevant classes in english and was in a city that i found interesting and would like to live in. All of this was applicable to Karolinska Institutet and Stockholm, which is why this ended up as my first priority when applying and why i was happy to accpet the spot when I was offered the spot here.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: KI was very good at guiding and welcoming new international students. We got plenty information before arriving and there was a whole week of welcome acitivities planned the week before the semester started. this included a wide range from both social activites to help with activating our student accounts and take picture for our student ID's.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above there was a whole week of welcome activites and study fairs planned. It was always easy to find a faculty member or international coordinator to ask if need be, and KI was very good at having all nessicary information available online, either on their social media or on their webpage.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
KI housing offeres a range of different housing around stockholm but only one on campus at the Solna campus, which is where all my classes were. It is fairly new student housing where you have the option to either live with a shared kitchen in your own room or in a shared apartment with either 2-4 people. Lastly the option for a studio with own kitchen was also available, but it was a bit more expensive than the former two options.

It is more expensive than the other housing offered to exchange students at KI but it is definelty worth it to live close to campus and the facilities are very nice since the housing was finished in 2019.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there was the option for either a shared kitchen with 10-18 other people, own kitchen or shared apartment 2-4 people with kitchen. No option for meal plans were available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The housing at Solna is an amazing opportunity to find friends and create a community while on exchange at KI. You are obviously not guareenteed great roommates, but i regret now that i didn't choose to share an apartment and instead had my own room with a big shared kitchen. 

either option is a good choice and the common areas in the buiding means that you have plenty oppotunity to host a game night or watch a movie together with friends. 

it is close to nice parks and with easy access to public transportation, so i was very satisfied with my choice to stay on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There is an online application form you fill out on KI's version of mobility online. You have to create a seperate log in to use for their mobility online. Here you fill in your prefeered classes (you have to be aware that they offer limited options for classes when you go on exchange in the biomedicine programme) in a prioritised order and then you send them in though this online form. 

after they have oficially accpeted you, then you will recieve a letter of acceptance showing what classes you got. this letter is also nessicary to apply for housing through KI housing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a zoom-meeting with all incoming exchange students in the biomedicine programme before application deadlines with plenty options to ask questions about the process as well as the option to reach out to your individual international coordinatior.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got both the classes i wanted as my first priority.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
make sure you study classes thoroughly beforehand to ensure its a good fit with what you want to learn and what your interest are. 

I did not have the best experience with the class in molecular medicine - cardiometabolic and infectious diseases, but i wanted to do the two 5th semester courses offered. In the future i would still have picked the oncology course offered on the 5th semester, but considered either doing a project or 3rd semeste courses for the remaining 15 credits of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
both classes were fail/pass which means that the amount of details nessicary to remember to pass were way less than what I have been used to a UCPH. 

I did not find them more or as academically challenging as the classes i have had in Copenhagen, but i still enjoyed most lectures and seminars and i feel i gained new skills and knowledge from my exhange.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it is very similar with a combination of small group work and classroom sessions combined with lectures and seminars. There were more assignments and deadlines of papers that had to be handed in than i have been used to at UCPH, but the student-professor dynamic is very similar and very grounded in the scandinavian teaching-style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Molecular medicine - Oncology
Molecular medicine - cardiometabolic and infectious diseases

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Molecular medicine - oncology 
it was an extremly well planned and cohesive couse that offered a better introduction to the clinical aspects of biomedicine that we dont get with the courses we have in copehangen. At the same time, most professors and teachers were amazing educators and gave great lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not have any unexpected costs during my exchange.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: groceries and lesiure activites like café visits were cheaper than expected, and cheaper than copenhagen. I expected my living-expenses to be comparable with Copenhagen, but i spend less on both rent and food in Stockholm. This might be due to the fact that the swedish Krone was fairly weak compared to the danish Krone while i was on exhcange

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a free gym available on the Solna campus that you can acess every day of the week. On top of this the student union plans different activites such as vollyball or badminton or yoga that you can sign up for and participate in for free if you want to. 

The different student union also plans parties and activities so keep an eye out on KI's social media and you will for sure find something to participate in!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I participated in the Students Noble Night Cap, which is the official afterparty after the nobel ceremony planned and hosted by students. It was a lot of work and you have to be prepared to spend a lot of time on it, but it was a fun way to meet sudents from other programmes and universities in Stockholm, and you might even get the chance to meet a real noble lauerate!

I would also definetly recommend that you buy a ticket for the lucia ball in december. It is a white tie event with music, dancing and a fancy dinner. Its a fun way to end your exchange year and a great excuse to get dressed up in a fancy dress or suit.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Stockholm has a lot of amazing day-hikes all within a short bus ride from the city center, so i would definelty recommend that you travel out of the city center in the early fall while the weather is great to experience the beautifull nature. 

ESN Stockholm host som amazing hikes every other weekend in the summer and fall which is a good choice if you don't want to plan a trip on your own. 

If you have the time and money, then travel up north to swedish lapland and see northern lights, experience true winter darkness and wilderness in a way we can't really get back home in Denmark - i sadly didnt have time but many of my friends left for lapland-trips and they all loved it. Beware that it is quite expensive, but well worth it!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Since sweden is not that different from Denmark it wasn't a massive cultural shit to move to Stockholm. 

The biggest change came in meeting fellow international students who came from very different cultures from all over the world. This was especially clear when working in groups or preparing presentations, since not all were equally used to that type of teaching and to be in charge of own learning in that way.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At times the language barrier talking with other students who's english was not always as developed and who were not as used to working the independently could at times be challenging. You learn to have to communicate clearly and set boundaries to ensure that its a nice work-enviroment for everyone - which will definetly be a benefit long term.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: fika! the mandatory almost daily coffe and cake/bun break, ensuring socialising and breaking down barriers between teacher and student, resident students and exchange students ect. It's a wonderfull tradition and something i will definetly bring home to Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Seize all opportunities that come to you

consider doing a project and not just courses while at KI - they have amazing professors and reseachers and you get a chance to work directly with them. 

Stay on campus! it makes your life 100 times easier and you will get to participate in all on-campus activites a lot easier.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting students from other european countries and learning about other european cultures - i now have friends spread all over europe and the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At times it can feel quite lonely, and you need to put in a lot of effort to create the same sense of community and belonging that I had at UCPH. I definetly learned a lot about myself and my need for social interactions and close friendships that i hadn't realised before i left for exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
